purpose: Read-only evidence for a possible PRM replacement; not authorization to replace a running model or to launch scoring/training.

judgment.recommendation: First screen the already available Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B on a fixed current-rollout offline acceptance set; do not switch live training or claim it is better yet.
judgment.qwen_better_on_current_three: unknown; no scores exist in the inspected artifacts

skipped_batches.policy: Exclude the entire 32-row batch from advantage replay; retain all raw scoring

historical_limitations: 288 rows selected as nine full historical batches containing empty answers; not representative sampling.
All raw scores retained. Whole B:210 batch excluded only from token-advantage replay because one reconstructed response exceeds fixed width.
Old logs did not save emitted token IDs; reconstruction with logged-length agreement still does not prove exact original tokens.
KL fixed to zero; this is an offline counterfactual, not historical A/B advantages or a prediction of future training.
Native-input formats differ by PRM. Raw-question and official-RL-prompt variants use shared canonical steps, not the official literal token splitter.
Final-answer concordance is not process correctness; there are no new human step labels.
No winner selected, no training launched, no reward or answer-verification rules changed.
interpretation: This was a selected historical set, not a random sample of current policy rollouts.
Outcome concordance is final-answer ranking, not step-level mathematical correctness.
Qwen and PURE both scored all nine empty rows positively; Qwen scored each empty row first within its group.
Some historical short incorrect outputs receive lower Qwen scores than PURE, others receive higher scores; no uniform improvement is established.
Historical advantage replay used the veRL signal family with reconstructed actor IDs and KL=0; it is not the current OpenRLHF exact-token boundary-mask result.
Historical A/B skipped PRM on empty responses and assigned zero reward, so this audit does not establish the cause of old B versus A accuracy.

current_three_matching.completion: I'm sorry, I cannot provide the answer without more context or a specific question related to the problem. Could you please provide the details of the problem?

interface_requirements.historical_comparison: Same canonical text steps, but each model native serialization; PURE also had a prompt-sensitivity variant. Historical original actor-emitted token IDs were unavailable.
interface_requirements.current_pilot: Saved original emitted actor token IDs, official process_sequences, exact actor boundary positions, native BF16 PRM transform, and full OpenRLHF signal/loss path.
qwen_native: Use Qwen own tokenizer and official chat template: system instruction, user question, assistant step strings joined and ended by <extra_0>.
Read the two-class logits at verified marker IDs; retain native dtype outputs plus FP32 diagnostic copies separately.
Retain original actor IDs/positions and saved old/reference log-probabilities. Do not reconstruct actor sequences by retokenizing decoded full text.

Construct and verify an explicit one-to-one mapping between the fixed original mathematical steps and score positions. Do not silently change the splitter, truncate input, or force PURE newline serialization on Qwen.

If necessary native adapters expose different step content or boundaries, disclose and separate that sensitivity. This is a model-plus-required-native-adapter replacement, not a causal comparison of weights alone.
Qwen card reports positive probability; converting its logits with the unchanged PURE signed/softmin transform is a declared replacement ablation, not the official PURE released PRM baseline.

input_sets: Discovery/regression: all 32 responses of the current batch2, including complete same-question groups and all three identified failure cases.
Independent confirmation: preselect complete saved 32-response batch(es) before seeing candidate scores, covering normal solutions, short correct answers, mixed groups and same-outcome groups.
Historical 288 text-only rows remain supplementary; keep their reconstruction limits separate.
fixed_controls: No new generation, no changes to verifier, original actor token IDs, valid/boundary masks, prompt/question text, grouped membership or saved old/reference logps.
Use each model documented native input serialization; do not tune prompts or segmentation after observing scores.
Replay exactly the current OpenRLHF signed score, softmin temperature0.1, actual peer-length baseline, KL0.001, boundary mask and normalization once; retain P_VR unchanged.
Keep the current running pilot untouched; any eventual replacement is a separately named experiment.
primary_checks: Interface gate: score-marker and actor-boundary mapping fully verified, no silent omissions or reconstruction failures.

Known-invalid regression gate: check whether the three answer-only wrong/refusal examples cease to receive positive response-mean advantage under unchanged full-group replay, rather than merely receiving smaller p scores.
Confirm the change on separately preselected complete batches and audited invalid cases; do not select a model solely because it passes the three discovered examples.
Check preservation of sensible signals on correct short answers and verified correct steps; a uniform downward score shift that also suppresses correct reasoning is not an improvement.
secondary_checks: Report false positive/false negative scoring on audited examples; report final-answer concordance only as a secondary proxy.
Report process scores, peer baselines, KL, raw returns and normalized response-mean advantages separately.
Stratify by all-correct/all-wrong/mixed groups and length/empty/short/refusal/truncation, preserving every original response.
Report paired differences and uncertainty on the independent set; failure-case examples cannot estimate population error rates.
Record inference time, input tokens, and peak memory in a future authorized scoring pass; offline ranking alone cannot certify downstream RL reliability.
proposed_offline_acceptance.decision_rule: Pass the interface and regression gates, avoid material regression on correct examples, and corroborate on the independent set before proposing a separately authorized training replacement. A failed gate is a rejection of this candidate/interface, not permission to add filters or new rewards.

candidates.role: Available local checkpoint; bounded offline screening first
Optional reserve only; not recommended to download or run before the existing Qwen screen

supports: Native chat serialization has system/user/assistant roles, inserts <extra_0> after every step, and scores positive class at each marker.
Recommended steps use double newlines for Qwen2.5-Math-Instruct responses.
This card reports BoN and ProcessBench, not a guarantee against optimization-driven reward hacking.
BoN may reward answer-correct but process-wrong responses and can overstate process verification quality.
Minimum scores can concentrate on final answer steps.
Strong inference-time learned reward models may fail to help or harm RL training; experiments document reward hacking.
A public 7B PRM with official inference code; reported evaluations include BoN@64 with averaged step rewards.
Not evidence that this model fixes this project current three failures.
Own prepare_input, reward flags and derive_step_rewards interface must be audited if ever used.
